feedback:
Accepted. The machine is well-formed and faithful to the stated task ('get to the exit, preferably holding the box on at least two different moves/steps').

Format: all required headers present (REWARD_MACHINE, STATES, INITIAL_STATE, FINAL_STATES, TRANSITION_FUNCTION, REWARD_FUNCTION). FINAL_STATES is nonempty (u3), declared in STATES, and accepting for the task (u3 = exit reached, the episode-terminal condition). All transition targets are declared states; each reward is attached to a matching (state, condition, next_state) triple; unrewarded else self-loops default to 0 per paper convention.

Coverage and ordering: per-state conditions are pairwise disjoint and exhaustive - (at_exit & holding_box), (at_exit & !holding_box), (!at_exit & holding_box), else partition all labelings in u0/u1; (at_exit)/else in u2; else in u3. Irrelevant events (siren_ringing, switch_toggled, box_fell) never appear in formulas and are absorbed by the per-state else self-loops at zero reward, as required. Only persistent conditions (at_exit, holding_box) are used; the event propositions are not misused as if persistent, and at_exit is correctly treated as the last-step trigger.

Reachability and compactness: u0->u1->u2->u3 is reachable whenever a box exists; in no-box (or siren-only) setups the direct (u0, at_exit)->u3 rule still reaches the final state and pays the full 1.0, so the machine degrades gracefully across all four setups. Four states is minimal for counting hold-steps 0/1/>=2 plus a terminal.

Reward safety and fidelity: no positive cycles; the only rewarded transitions are the two one-shot progress steps (0.1 each) and the exit, bounding the maximum return at 1.2 (dense progress, bounded total). Case analysis confirms the preference is strictly encoded: 0 hold-steps -> 1.0; exactly 1 hold-step then exit unheld -> 1.1; >=2 hold-steps -> 1.2. Exiting while holding forces >=2 hold-steps (after pickup the agent faces the box, and any holding non-exit step advances the counter), so the orderings align with 'at least two different moves.' Sticky u1/u2 are correct because the preference is historical - the task does not require holding at exit, so no regression edges are needed, and box_fell during u2 is correctly absorbed by the else loop without undoing progress.

Minor non-blocking remarks: the two rules paying 1.1 on (at_exit & holding_box) from u0/u1 are unreachable - holding at the exit step implies a prior holding non-exit step, which already advanced the counter - so every satisfying exit actually pays 0.2 progress + 1.0; these dead rules could be pruned for compactness but are harmless and do not affect the preference ordering. The flat 1.0/1.1 exit rewards intentionally abstract away the environment's time-dependent payoff (1 - 0.9 * fraction of limit used), which propositional RM conditions cannot express; this is consistent with the task line, which specifies no speed condition.
